The test image shows banana fruit (pods) with dark brown/black necrotic lesions on the fruit surface. The lesions are on the body of the fruit, not at the tips.

Key observations:
- Affected part: fruit/pod
- Dark, irregular necrotic patches covering large areas of the fruit surface
- Multiple fruit affected, lesions appear on the sides/body (not tips)

From the class list, only **Anthracnose** and **Cigar_End_Rot** have pod-level reference images. Cigar End Rot typically causes dry rot at the fruit tip/end. The lesions here are on the body of the fruit, pointing toward Anthracnose.

Let me view the Anthracnose pod reference image.

The Anthracnose reference shows small dark spots on the fruit body. The test image shows larger, more coalesced dark necrotic patches on the fruit surface — consistent with a more advanced stage of Anthracnose where spots have merged. The key discriminating factor is location: lesions are on the fruit body (not the tip), ruling out Cigar End Rot. The dark necrosis on the pod/fruit surface matches Anthracnose.
